paper.title: Competing Bandits in Matching Markets via Super Stability

unmapped: two-sided matching market with N users and K arms (N <= K), both sides have unknown preferences (two-sided uncertainty)
action is a matching; each matched pair (user, arm) observes noisy rewards on both sides
regret is pessimal stable regret / binary stable regret (rounds where matching is not stable)
central platform forms the matching from reported partial ranks
settings.definition_quote: We consider the matching markets with two-sided uncertainty. There are $N$ users and $K$ arms... where $\eta_{i,j}(t)$ and $\eta'_{j,i}(t)$ are independent $1$-subgaussian noise... Centralized: In this setting, in each round the arms and users reveal their learned preferences to a central platform.

settings.name_in_paper: Decentralized two-sided matching bandit (2 shared flags)
unmapped: two-sided matching market with two-sided uncertainty, N <= K
users propose to arms; arms accept at most one; collisions give zero reward
regret is pessimal stable regret / binary stable regret
settings.definition_quote: Decentralized: In this setting, in each round the users can propose to the arms (possibly multiple). Each arm can accept and match with at most one user... Additionally, users have access to 2 shared flags (binary semaphores).

settings.name_in_paper: Centralized two-sided matching bandit, Bernoulli rewards (lower bound)
unmapped: two-sided matching market, parameter theta=(mu,gamma) in [0,1]^{2NK}
binary stable regret: number of rounds with a non-stable matching
settings.definition_quote: Our system is parameterized by $\theta = (\boldsymbol{\mu}, \boldsymbol{\gamma}) \in \Theta := [0,1]^{2 N K}$. We focus on Bernoulli rewards with appropriate means for ease of exposition.

algorithms.name: Centralized Two-Sided Matching Bandit (UCB-LCB partial ranks + Extended Gale-Shapley, round-robin exploration)

symbols.Delta_A: admissible gap: largest minimum gap over admissible partial ranks

source.label: thm:centralized_main
source.quote: The cumulative regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg:centralized} in $T$ rounds for the true stable matching instance with no ties $(F^*_{u}, F^*_{a})$ satisfies ... \mathbb{E}[R_{0/1}(T)] \leq (K + \frac{NK \pi^2}{3} + \frac{96 K\log(T)}{\Delta^2_{\mathcal{A}}})

results.notes: Bound on expected binary stable regret (number of rounds without a stable matching). Theorem also states that each user's/arm's pessimal stable regret normalized by (mu_pess - mu_min) is at most E[R_{0/1}(T)]. Algorithm uses log(t) so treated as anytime.

source.label: thm:decentralized_main
source.quote: For a true stable matching instance $(F^*_{u}, F^*_{a})$ when the users follow Algorithm~\ref{alg:decentralizedUser}, and the arms follow Algorithm~\ref{alg:decentralizedArm}, the cumulative regret in $T$ rounds satisfies ... \mathbb{E}[R_{0/1}(T)] \leq (1 + N^2 + K + \frac{NK \pi^2}{3} + \frac{96 K\log(T)}{\Delta^2_{\mathcal{A}}})

results.notes: Binary stable regret; per user/arm pessimal stable regret normalized is bounded by it as well.

symbols.c_theta: value of the Graves-Lai type LP over matchings with bad set Lambda(theta) defined through admissible partial ranks

source.label: thm:centralized_lower
source.quote: For any instance $\theta \in \Theta$, for any {\em uniformly good} policy $\pi$ the binary stable regret is lower bounded as $\lim\inf_{T\to \infty} \frac{\mathbb{E}[R_{0/1}^{\pi}(T; \theta)]}{\log(T)} \geq c(\theta)$, where $c(\theta)$ minimizes the following optimization problem ...

results.notes: Adapted from Combes et al. / Graves & Lai framework (also stated as Theorem F.1).

symbols.c_u_max: max_i c_{u,i}, c_{u,i}=sum_{j in D_i} 1/kl(gamma_{j,i},gamma_{j,j}) + sum_{j>i} 1/kl(mu_{i,j},mu_{i,i})
symbols.c_a_max: max_j c_{a,j}, c_{a,j}=sum_{i: j in D_i} 1/kl(gamma_{j,i},gamma_{j,j}) + sum_{i<j} 1/kl(mu_{i,j},mu_{i,i})

conditions: general serial dictatorship instance: gamma_{j,i} > gamma_{j,i'} for i<i' for all arms j

source.quote: Consider a general serial dictatorship instance $\theta$ with two sided uncertainty, where $N\leq K$, $\gamma_{j,i}(\theta) > \gamma_{j,i'}(\theta)$ for all $i < i'$ and $j$, and the unique stable matching is $\{(i,i): i \in [N]\}$. Then the binary stable regret ... is lower bounded as ... \geq \max(\max_{i}c_{u,i}(\theta), \max_{j}c_{a,j}(\theta))

results.notes: Binary stable regret liminf ratio to log T.

symbols.c_a_max: max over unlocked arms j of sum_{i} 1/kl(mu_{i,j}, mu_{i,j*(i)})

source.quote: Consider a general two-sided stable matching instance $\theta$ with redundant arms $N < K$, where $j^*(i) \triangleq \max_{j}\{ \mu_{i,j}(\theta): (i,j) \in Locked(\theta)\}$. Then the binary stable regret ... is lower bounded as ...

results.notes: j*(i) is the best locked arm of user i.

symbols.c_CG: max over non-connected cover groups G of sum_{C in G} 1/kl(theta,C)

source.label: thm:centralized_lower_final
source.quote: The value of $c(\theta)$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:centralized_lower_combes} is lower bounded by the value $c_{\varepsilon}(\theta)$ ... Furthermore, $c(\theta)$ satisfies the following lower bound $c(\theta) \geq \max_{G \in \mathcal{CG}(\theta)}\sum_{C\in G} kl(\theta, C)^{-1}$

results.notes: Combined with Theorem 5.1 gives liminf binary stable regret / log T >= this quantity.
